# Signal registry

<!-- Generated by scripts/build-signals.mjs. Edit signals/registry.json, then npm run build. -->

Registry **1.6.0**, detector **1.6.0**. [Machine-readable registry](../signals/registry.json) · [JSON Schema](../signals/registry.schema.json)

Versioned evidence catalogue, not runtime configuration. validated is scoped to the listed verification, not population accuracy. Code status governs emission; token/element status describes product evidence. Retired legacy UA literals can remain compatible with an active output code when retirementReason explicitly records this. Unknown version ranges must stay explicit. Consent replay is publication metadata only: one late analytics_storage grant update can replay the latest result as final with traffic_replay=consent; no scoring signal or persisted consent state.

Registry families group evidence as environment, behaviour, declaration and carry-over. `scoringFamily` is the separate runtime correlation cap; weights are implemented defaults, not probabilities. Hard/inherited/declaration weights of 100 are sentinels. Ordinary soft evidence requires the corroboration rules in [How it works](how-it-works.md#signals); UB and AW window profiles with missing WebGL and another corroborator have direct suspicious rules; strong AW is excluded from CS provenance checks.

`observed` means the listed limited field runs were observed, without prevalence validation. CP/KT/TG directly yield suspicious and seed one-document CS after their thresholds; never automation or identity. `experimental` means upstream evidence or release coverage remains incomplete. `validated` means only the listed code, documentation or observation was checked, not a population accuracy claim. Unknown product versions are recorded explicitly; synthetic fixtures do not validate a real product release.

A retired **output code** must not be emitted. A retired **token** records an ended operator identity; its old literal may remain in the unchanged detector and emit the active AG code. Google-NotebookLM is this compatibility case. Claude light-DOM markers remain experimental with limited historical coverage; 1.0.107 is a recorded negative result, not a claim that historical matches stopped working.

Build regenerates this page deterministically; `npm run test:registry` validates the schema, checks source inventories and weights, rejects retired output codes, and warns when any last check is more than 120 days old. Dates are evidence review dates, never automatically refreshed by build. Add a source and honest product/version scope for every new entry.
